(5) When the content gives rise to a suspicion under DSA Art. 18, the bullet above applies on its own terms.
````markdown
- **The yearly count.** Each January the operator counts the past calendar year's decisions marked terrorist content (with the reviews and corrections that reversed them) and the orders in their own records, and publishes the TCO Art. 7(2) report before 1 March when it applies.
- **The users' contact mailbox** (`WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL`). The operator reads it at least each working day, in a mail client set to load no remote content and to show no inline image or attachment preview. Attachments are never opened, previewed, downloaded or forwarded, and no link in a mail is followed: a korbat link is copied into the report form, never opened. Every report or notice found there is entered through the report form, signed out in a private window, from the mail's text alone, with the sender's links, ground, rule or category, explanation and cited law, and, for a notice that is not on the path for child sexual abuse material, the sender's name and email; the good-faith box is ticked only when the mail states the sender's good-faith belief that it is accurate and complete. It is stored as any report sent without an account, so the sender gets `notice_received` with the status link, the daily `notice_update` and re-examination. A mail that says it concerns the sexual abuse or exploitation of a child, child sexual abuse material or the grooming of a child is entered on the third ground of the form, with the choice its words name ("Sexual images or videos of a child" when they name none) and without the sender's name or email. When the entered report carries no contact (a rule-only report, for which the form asks no name or email, or the third ground), the sender gets the fixed reply with the reference and the status page's link from the success screen. The mail is then deleted with its attachments and removed from the trash the same day; the fixed reply that carries a reference of the third ground is deleted from the sent folder, and from the trash, once sent. A finding is never used for a mailed report or notice: it would say "found by a moderator" and send no receipt or decision. A mail from an authority is handled as the bullet on authorities' orders says, its attachment opened only after step 1 has verified the sender. No report or notice is answered by hand except with the three fixed replies below; the only other mails sent from this address are the GDPR answers (below) and the answers to an authority's order; at most 20 reports can be entered a day from one network (5 an hour), and while Turnstile is down they wait. The fixed replies:
  - asking for the good-faith sentence, or for the form: "korbat received your email. To handle it as a notice that something on korbat is illegal, korbat needs your statement that you believe in good faith that the information in it is accurate and complete. Reply with that sentence, or send your report through the form at <the app's address>/report, which asks for it. korbat's emails never discuss a case."
  - giving the reference and the status link: "korbat entered your report. Its reference is <reference>. To see where it stands, or to ask for a re-examination of a decision, open this page: <the link from the success screen>. Keep the link: korbat cannot show it again. korbat has deleted your email, and deletes this reply."
  - to a mail about a decision: "korbat answers a decision only through its own procedures: the person a decision restricts can appeal it in korbat under Settings, Cases, and a person who reported can ask for a re-examination of a decision to take no action on the page their receipt links to, or under Settings, Cases, Your reports, within six months of being told. korbat's emails never discuss a case."
- **"Illegal on the face of it" and "not evident".** A notice gives korbat knowledge only if it lets a diligent host see the illegality without a detailed legal examination (DSA Art. 16(3), recital 22), and each restriction must be diligent, objective and proportionate, with due regard to freedom of expression (Art. 14(4)). So a notice of illegality has three answers. Illegal on the face of it: restrict without delay on the legal ground, and the statement cites the law. Not illegal: "No breach". Not evident without a detailed legal examination: "Illegality not evident", a lawful answer that leaves the content up until a court or an authority orders otherwise; its sender is told, and can ask once for a re-examination, go to court or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator. It is a liability decision made case by case: should a court later find the content illegal and find that korbat knew, the hosting exemption of Art. 6 is gone for that item, so a moderator in doubt asks the operator before answering. A removal on the law names the law, never a rule, and is counted apart from removals under the rules.
- **The statement's texts** (facts, reason, legal reference, review reason) never hold personal data of anyone but the author: describe it ("the home address of another person"), never copy it, since they are mailed, exported and kept while the account exists, also after an R4 redaction has erased the content. A saved draft that copies it is not confirmed: save a corrected one. The API refuses a text that quotes what a reporter or notifier wrote on the case (`text_quotes_user`).
- **Tools.** Machine translation stays local. The console runs in a browser profile of its own with no extensions, and nothing from it is pasted into third-party tools. The daily limits on cases and reveals are raised with `staff.js limits` when honest work reaches them, and the new numbers go into the operator's records.
- **A `staff_recused` refusal** may mean one of the case's reporters is close to your own account: do not try to learn which, and leave the case to another staff member. When no other staff member can take it (with one staff member, always), the case waits in the queue and its lane-0 and queue-age mails keep coming, and the operator makes another person staff (grant-role and enrolment) to decide it. Nobody unlinks an account, or unfollows, unmutes or unblocks one, to get round a refusal.
- **A case about a staff account's content or profile fields.** Every final restrictive measure on a staff account is refused (`staff_target`): staff are disciplined by demotion. Whoever is on duty withholds the post or image, seals reported images, or resets the field, while deciding, as for any account, and tells the operator, who makes the account a user with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm api node dist/grant-role.js <email> user` (which ends its staff keys and sessions), after which a moderator who is not a party decides the case.
- **Mails that wait or were given up.** A count of waiting mails that stays above zero means the relay cannot take mail: check the API log for `MailUnavailable`; if it shows none, the dispatch fails before the send (its daily step, or a contact it cannot read): read the API log for `moderation-dispatch` and fix it the same day. A count of mails given up means the relay answered that an address does not exist (RFC 3463 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.1.3, 5.1.6 or 5.1.10), or a mail stayed unsent for five days; korbat does not try it again, the person still sees the outcome on the status page or in the app, and the API log names each one (`moderation: mail given up`). A relay that refuses korbat itself (relaying denied, missing credentials, a sender it refuses, a quota) raises the count of waiting mails instead, with `MailUnavailable` in the log: fix `API_SMTP_URL` or the relay within five days and nothing is lost.
- **Decisions not released, and late erasures.** The home screen shows either count only when it is above zero, with the sentence that stands here. A count of decisions not released means the daily release keeps failing: notifiers are not told and re-examination windows do not open, so read the API log for `moderation-dispatch` and fix it the same day. A count of late erasures names the due rule whose step keeps failing, so evidence, an intake record or a notifier's name and address outlives its published period: read the API log for `moderation-retention` and for `auth janitor: purge failed`, and check that `API_MODERATION_RETENTION` was not left `off` after a restore (the API logs it at every start).
- **A GDPR access request at the contact address.** Confirm that the requester holds the account (a mail from its address) or the email (the answer goes only to that address); run `staff.js access-request`; for every case it marks for the authorities' check, look in your R2, Art. 18 and order records. A case still open with a lane-0 item first goes through its R2 or Art. 18 step. For a case reported to an authority, or one an order concerns, ask that authority whether telling the person now would harm its work, and hold that case's part of the answer until it answers or counsel advises (GDPR Art. 23(1)(d) and the national law that applies; DSA Art. 9(5), 10(5)), within the periods of Art. 12(3); a person decides each item marked for weighing and records why; reply within one month (GDPR Art. 12(3)), saying what was withheld and why; keep the draft with the reply for the period counsel sets, since a withheld item may have to go before the supervisory authority or a court (C-203/22). Any other request under GDPR Articles 16 to 22 at the contact address: confirm the requester as for an access request; answer within one month (Art. 12(3)), saying what korbat did or, when it does nothing, why, and that the person may complain to a supervisory authority or go to court (Art. 12(4)); evidence that a case still needs is kept (GDPR Art. 17(3)(b) and (e), 21(1)). No answer names a reporter or notifier, quotes a report or a notice, or says whether a given person reported.
- **After each deploy and each week** the operator runs `staff.js text-verify` with `audit-verify`.

Records the operator keeps off the server, beside 3a's list of staff: each staff member's linked personal handles, updated at every `staff.js link` and `unlink`; every R2 report with the post's or the account's address, the case, the seal's time and the authority's reference; what `staff.js account-facts` printed for a case on that path, kept until the admin's answer and destroyed after an answer without a seal; every act done by hand on sealed files on an authority's written instruction (what, when, on which instruction); every notification under Art. 18 or TCO Art. 14(5), as its bullet lists it; every authority's order received, its verification, the answers sent and what was done; and the numbers last set with `staff.js limits`.

## Profile and account
Signed-in accounts manage themselves under Settings; every route below needs the session and, where it says fresh, a re-authentication within five minutes (the app opens its panel when the API answers `reauth_required`).
- **Profile.** `PATCH /api/me/profile` sets the display name (up to 50 characters) and the bio (one line, up to 160). `POST /api/me/handle` (fresh) changes the handle once every 30 days; every handle an account ever had stays reserved for it in `handle_history`, so nobody else can take an old handle and the account can go back to it, except a handle korbat retired, which is nobody's, its former holder's included; a retirement lifts the 30-day wait (Moderation, Handle retirement). There is no redirect from an old handle.
- **Email.** `POST /api/auth/email/change/start` (fresh) sends a code to the new address; `POST /api/auth/email/change/verify` moves the account there and tells the old address, whose notice carries a link (`/email-revert/<token>`, `POST /api/auth/email/revert`, valid 24 hours, once) that moves the account back and runs the lockdown described under Passkeys and fresh authentication (every session and device signed out, the password removed, passkeys and two-factor authentication set up since the day before the change removed). Sessions stay signed in after a change.
- **Verified badge.** Proof of holding a phone number, kept only as a keyed hash; one number per account. `VERIFY_PROVIDER` picks who sends the text: `off` (default; the badge is hidden), `dev` (the code is always `000000`; refused in production) or `vonage` (Vonage Verify v2 with `VONAGE_API_KEY`, `VONAGE_API_SECRET` and `VERIFY_BRAND`; the runbook is section 13 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-24-account-lifecycle-1b-design.md`, and `node scripts/verify-badge.mjs +4479xxxxxxxx` checks live credentials without touching an account). Routes: `POST /api/auth/badge/start`, `POST /api/auth/badge/verify`, `DELETE /api/auth/badge` (all fresh); starts are limited per account, per number, per IP and instance-wide (200 texts a day), and a flow takes at most five codes. The web build shows the badge section only with `WEB_BADGE=on` in `infra/.env` (the default is off, matching `API_VERIFY_PROVIDER=off`); set both together.
- **Data export.** `POST /api/account/export` (fresh, once a day) streams a ZIP with `export.json` (the account with its passkeys' names and dates, profile, posts, likes, reposts, bookmarks, following, blocks, mutes, sessions, devices and security events, and last the member `moderation`: the decisions about the account as its Cases screen lists them, with their statements while korbat holds them, and the reports the account sent, with their outcomes once released; since account sanctions also its strikes, suspensions, terminations and reporting measures, its replies to them and its own reporting counts, and in the profile the handles korbat retired) and every image the account uploaded under `media/`, except sealed images, images of posts it deleted and images whose content was erased, which are in neither the list nor the files. It never holds another person's report, a reporter, a notifier or a staff handle. Nothing is kept on the server: the archive is written entry by entry (ZIP64 when it passes 4 GiB or 65,535 entries), `export.json` is read in pages and streamed last, image files go through the media module's checked open, a request that fails before the first byte gives the day's export back, and one that fails midway breaks the download instead of saving a truncated archive.
- **Deletion.** `POST /api/account/delete/start` (fresh) mails a code; `POST /api/account/delete/confirm` with the code and the handle typed by the owner deletes the account at once: every session is revoked, posts become tombstones with their images and any pending uploads deleted from disk, likes, reposts, bookmarks, follows, blocks and mutes go with their counters, the profile is anonymised and keeps its handle, and the auth row is anonymised. The `account-purge` job (every five minutes) finishes any deletion the process did not, and takes down a terminated account once its decision is final for the person (Moderation, Termination). Nothing can be undone. A suspension, a termination or a seal never refuses or delays a person's own deletion. Moderation outlives a deletion: images that a case holds as evidence, or that an unanswered report of child sexual abuse material or a seal freezes, keep their rows and files, served to nobody, until nothing retains them; open cases about the account or its posts go on and are decided on their snapshots; the reports the account sent are still decided, with nothing left that says who sent them; and the statements of decisions about the account are erased 12 months after the deletion (Moderation, Evidence and retention).
## Passkeys and fresh authentication
An account can sign in and confirm sensitive changes with a passkey (WebAuthn), beside the emailed code, the password and two-factor codes. The API verifies through `@simplewebauthn/server`, which only `apps/api/src/auth/passkeys/webauthn.ts` imports; that module pins korbat's settings and adds its own checks.
- **Settings.** `API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` is the domain passkeys are bound to (default: the host of `API_APP_ORIGIN`) and `API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME` the name a browser shows (default `korbat`). Production refuses `localhost`, an IP address and anything that is not the origin's host or a parent domain of it. Browsers offer passkeys only on `https` or on `http://localhost`, never on an IP address.
- **Adding.** `POST /api/auth/passkeys/register/options` and `/verify`. Up to 10 passkeys, 5 added a day. User verification (fingerprint, face or PIN) is asked for and never required; only the attestation formats `none` and self-attested `packed` are accepted, so nothing is fetched from an authenticator's maker. The owner is mailed a link (`/passkey-remove/<token>`, valid 7 days, once) that removes the passkey and locks the account down.
- **Managing.** `GET /api/auth/passkeys` lists them (name, dates, synced, the device that added it, new, suspended); `PATCH /api/auth/passkeys/:id` renames and `DELETE` removes, the last one too. "This wasn't me" on a passkey of the last 7 days (`POST /api/auth/passkeys/:id/not-mine`) runs the lockdown.
- **Signing in.** `POST /api/auth/passkey/signin/options` and `/verify` need no email: the browser offers the passkeys it holds for the domain, from the button or from the email field's autofill. A sign-in whose passkey verified the user counts as two factors; one that did not is followed by the two-factor code on an account that has two-factor authentication, and staff who have it always give the code. A signature counter that goes backwards switches the passkey off, mails the owner and refuses the sign-in.
- **Fresh authentication has two levels.** A session records what it proved and when. Level 1 is any factor in the last five minutes; level 2 is a user-verified passkey, or a two-factor or recovery code beside an email code, a password or a passkey. An account with two-factor authentication needs level 2 to add or remove a passkey, change its password or email, set up, turn off or re-issue two-factor codes, and delete itself; every other account needs level 1. A refusal is `reauth_required` with `details: { level, have }`, and `POST /api/auth/reauth` (password, emailed code, two-factor code, recovery code or passkey) answers the level reached and rotates the session's token in place, so a copy of the old token stops working. Sessions are listed and revoked by an id that survives the rotation.
- **Lockdown.** Every "this wasn't me" runs one routine: the new-device alert's link, the passkey mail's remove link, the button on a new passkey, and the email change's undo. It signs out every session and device, removes the password, and removes the passkeys and two-factor authentication set up since the day before the event, in one transaction; the owner gets back in with a code sent to their email. A mailed link is tied to the address it went to: it does nothing while the account is at another address and works again once the address is restored.
- **What is kept.** The public key, the credential's id, its counter, whether it is synced and was registered with user verification, its name, and the device that added it; nothing about a fingerprint or a face ever leaves the person's device. The export lists names and dates only, and deleting the account deletes the passkeys.
- **After restoring a backup** the counters in the database are older than the authenticators': run `update auth.passkeys set counter = 0, suspect_at = null where suspect_at is null or suspect_at > '<restore time>';` so no passkey is refused as a copy (section 11 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-passkeys-1c-design.md`).
- **Tests.** A software authenticator (`apps/api/test/auth/soft-authenticator.ts`) runs whole ceremonies in the unit and integration suites. The API prints two `ExperimentalWarning`s at start, from the library's probe of Node 24's ML-DSA support; they are expected.
## Before going public
**The hard gate.** korbat is not opened to the public and sign-up is not opened to people the operator does not know until sub-project 3f's order path and sub-project 3d's handling of sealed images have both shipped, and no authorities' contact point is published until 3f's order path ships. The TCO Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2021/784) applies to a host insofar as it disseminates information to the public (Art. 1(2)) and its removal orders must be executed within one hour (Art. 3); DSA Art. 9 and 10 orders presuppose a service offered in the Union; 3c cannot meet either. 3c can seal images reported as child sexual abuse material, but it has no function to hand them over, to erase them or to carry a seal across a restore. Moving sub-project 4 before 3f or before 3d reopens this. The designs are `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-authorities-orders-3f-design.md` (the order path, the alert channel, the records of reports to authorities and the recovery after a restore) and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-account-sanctions-3e-design.md` (strikes, suspensions and handle retirement); the order of work is 3c, 3e, 3f, 3d.

Set these in `infra/.env`:
- `API_APP_ORIGIN` to the public origin, for example `https://korbat.example`; the API refuses a plain-http origin in production.
- `API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` and `WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` to the keys of one Turnstile widget; the API and the web build refuse Cloudflare's test keys in production.
- `API_SMTP_URL` and `API_MAIL_FROM` to the EU mail relay; a plain `smtp://` relay must offer STARTTLS, which the API requires in production.
- `API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` before the first passkey is registered, when it should differ from the host of `API_APP_ORIGIN`; changing it afterwards strands every passkey. The staff console does not use it: staff keys are bound to the console's own relying party ID.
- `API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN` to the staff console's public origin, for example `https://korbat-staff.example`, preferably on a registrable domain of its own so browsers treat the app and the console as different sites (a subdomain of the app's domain works too), and `API_CONSOLE_RP_ID` left empty, so staff keys are bound to that hostname. Production refuses a plain-http console, an IP address or `localhost`, the app's hostname on any port, a console on a parent domain of the app's hostname, and a relying party ID other than the console's hostname or equal to the app's; no environment accepts the console's origin in `API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`. Empty, the console is off. From sub-project 3c only the console decides reports and notices; with it off they are taken and wait, and staff are alerted to them.
- `WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL` to the users' contact address, which the report form names when the human check fails or the limits are reached and which the terms page shows; the web image refuses to build without one, and a production build refuses a placeholder (a domain ending in `.local`, `.localhost`, `.test`, `.invalid` or `.example`, or `example.com`, `example.org` or `example.net`). Its mailbox is set to load no remote content, and to keep deleted mail no longer than its host's shortest setting; a person reads it every working day (Moderation, the runbook's bullet on the users' contact mailbox). With sub-project 3f the authorities' contact address is published as well, with the languages it may be addressed in, among them an official language of korbat's home state (DSA Art. 11(3), TCO Art. 15(2)), and notified to the national authorities where the home state requires it.
- `API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR` to the hour of the UTC day, 0 to 23, at which the day's decisions on reports and notices are released to those who sent them, in one batch, so that nobody can tell from a mail's minute when a decision was made; empty means 7.
- `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` generated (`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` fills a placeholder), backed up off the server and rotated as the paragraph below says; `API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN=off` and `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on`, their defaults (Moderation says when each is changed).
- `KORBAT_ENV=production` before building the images; it is the API's `NODE_ENV` too, so the guards above are on.
- `TUNNEL=on` and `API_TRUST_PROXY=cloudflare` when cloudflared is the only way in (the app's public hostname points at `http://caddy:8080`, and the console's at `http://caddy:8090`, below); `TUNNEL=off` and `API_TRUST_PROXY=caddy` when Caddy's port is reachable directly. With `on`, Caddy keeps `CF-Connecting-IP` for the API; with `off` it drops it, so nobody can claim an address.
- In Cloudflare, set Browser Cache TTL to "Respect Existing Headers", or browsers keep images for four hours whatever the server says.

Keep `API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY`, `API_IP_HASH_KEY`, `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY` and `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` secret and backed up. Losing `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY` breaks every enrolled authenticator. To rotate it, put the old key in `API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS` and a new `v2:` key in `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY`; each secret is re-encrypted with the new key when it is next used. Without `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` korbat can neither mail a signed-out notifier nor say who sent a notice. To rotate `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY`, put the old key in `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS` and a new `v2:` key in `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY`. Contacts are never re-encrypted, so the old key stays listed until no contact made under it remains, that is until `select count(*) from auth.notifier_contacts where name_enc like 'v1:%' or email_enc like 'v1:%'` answers 0. A contact can outlive 13 months while its notice is still owed a decision or a mail. Keep the old key off the server for as long as any backup holds such a contact.

Before the first report can concern a threat to someone's life or safety, obtain and record the channels for a notification under DSA Art. 18: the national police's, and Europol's for when the Member State concerned cannot be identified, each asked for beforehand from the national police or the Digital Services Coordinator (Moderation, the runbook's bullet on Art. 18).

A post that a decision withholds or removes leaves Explore at the next read, as it leaves every list; nothing acts on Explore alone. Since formula version 2 (account sanctions) a post that a later decision restores gets back the hours it was hidden, and a suspended account's posts and approvals leave the round while the suspension runs. Explore's cold start lasts about two days: only accounts at least 48 hours old count, so on a new instance Explore stays empty until the first accounts are that old.

The staff console's final hostname is chosen before the first enrolment. Staff keys are bound to it, since `API_CONSOLE_RP_ID` equals it, so moving the console later strands every staff key and means a new enrolment for every person; this includes a move to a domain of its own or behind a gate at another hostname. The tunnel gets a second public hostname, the console's, pointing at `http://caddy:8090`, with its HTTP Host Header setting left empty, so the API sees the console's hostname. Cloudflare Access in front keeps the hostname and the keys. A WireGuard or Tailscale gate keeps them only if it serves the same hostname over https with a certificate of its own, because Caddy runs with `auto_https off` while TLS ends at Cloudflare. Rocket Loader, Zaraz and Web Analytics stay off for the console's hostname, through a configuration rule for that hostname: the console's policy would block every script they add. Each staff member enrols two keys.

Who can rewrite the audit log: the PostgreSQL superuser, the owner `korbat_migrate` (its password is in `infra/.env`, and the migrate service uses it at every start), and anyone with Docker access on the host (psql inside the postgres container is the superuser without a password). Any of them can change a row, recompute every later hash and move the head, and a plain `audit-verify` then passes; only a place kept before the change, by someone other than the person who made it, shows the change. Until sub-project 3d publishes the head, that is the kept-head practice of the runbook under Staff console: each day the keeper, the staff member who does not run the server, copies the newest place and hash from the console's audit page and opens the place kept on the previous visit with "Go to place" to check its hash, and after each deploy and each week the operator runs `audit-verify` with every place the keeper has kept. In 3a the keeper's check is the only one independent of the operator, and it still reads through the operator's API, so it detects a change made in the database, not one that also changes the API's code to show the kept hashes. With one person, nothing detects the operator's own changes until 3d. Run `audit-verify` before and after every PostgreSQL major upgrade: the chain's text embeds PostgreSQL's print of the stored JSON, and a version that printed it differently would fail every row with metadata, never pass a forged one.

Counsel's list, to be answered before the gate above opens. From moderation cases: the period for which the draft of an access request's answer is kept; whether a removal of terrorist content on a notice makes korbat a provider that has taken action under TCO Art. 7(2); whether a final decision on content its author already deleted is mailed; whether, and under which national law, an access request may be restricted or deferred for a case korbat reported to an authority under DSA Art. 18 or for images it sealed for good, or that an authority's order concerns (GDPR Art. 23(1)(d)), what the answer and any extension under Art. 12(3) then say, and whether it names those authorities as recipients (Art. 15(1)(c)); whether 30 days suits the content backups hold; and every question that section 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-moderation-cases-3c-design.md` flags for counsel on the path for child sexual abuse material (its rows Suspected child sexual abuse material, Evidence, What the author sees of removed content, and Case targets and measures). From account sanctions: every question that section 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-account-sanctions-3e-design.md` flags for counsel, among them the reply window and what counts as sent, the protective suspension on images nobody assessed, termination, the restriction of reporting and its counts, how long the ledger's rows are kept, the handle retired under R4, and that korbat holds no account against its deletion.

## Dependency audit

`pnpm audit --audit-level high` runs in CI. Two lower advisories are accepted, both in build-time tools that never see untrusted input here: `esbuild` 0.18 under drizzle-kit's config loader (its development server, which nothing starts) and `uuid` 7 under Expo's Xcode config plugin. Renovate moves them with their parents.
````

### Replace `apps/api/src/account/flows/export.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { STANDING_RULES, type Platform } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { AccountExport } from "../../auth";
import type { ModerationExport } from "../../moderation";
import type { ProfileExport } from "../../social";
import { AccountError, type AccountDeps } from "../context";
import type { OpenFile, ZipWriter } from "../zip";

/** One export a day (1b design, section 10). */
export const EXPORTS_PER_WINDOW = 1;
export const EXPORT_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

const exportLimitKey = (userId: string) => `export:${userId}`;

/** The entry an image has in the archive; export.json names it under the post's media. */
export function mediaEntry(id: string): string {
  return `media/${id}.webp`;
}

/** The download's name: the handle and the day, so several exports of one account sort by date. */
export function exportFilename(handle: string, now: Date): string {
  return `korbat-export-${handle}-${now.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}.zip`;
}

/**
 * What the archive is written from. The account's own facts, the profile and the moderation member are
 * read before the first byte; the profile's lists are read page by page while export.json is written,
 * and the images, each behind the media module's checked open, go first, so `missingMedia` is complete
 * by the time the JSON that lists it is written.
 */
export interface ExportPlan {
  exportedAt: Date;
  /** The handle of the session that asked for the export: the id the auth module lists each session under. */
  currentSession: string;
  account: AccountExport;
  profile: ProfileExport;
  /** The decisions about the account that it was told of and its own reports, as the moderation module hands them over (3c design, section 7.11). */
  moderation: ModerationExport;
  images: { id: string; open: OpenFile }[];
  /** The images whose file the checked open refused or could not find, filled while the images are written. */
  missingMedia: string[];
}

/**
 * Counts one export of the account in the daily window and refuses once it is used up. Taken before
 * anything is built or streamed, so a stream that fails midway still counts; Retry-After says when the
 * window resets.
 */
export async function enforceExportLimit(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string): Promise<void> {
  let hit: { count: number; resetMs: number };
  try {
    hit = await deps.limits.hit(exportLimitKey(userId), EXPORT_WINDOW_MS);
  } catch {
    // Fails closed: an export that cannot be counted is not made, and the client is told to retry shortly.
    throw new AccountError("service_unavailable", 503, undefined, 30);
  }
  if (hit.count > EXPORTS_PER_WINDOW) throw new AccountError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, Math.max(1, Math.ceil(hit.resetMs / 1000)));
}

/**
 * Gives the day's export back after a failure before the archive's first byte (a pool timeout, a
 * restart): the owner received nothing, so the attempt must not use up the day. Best effort: when the
 * store cannot be reached, the export stays counted and a warning says so, which costs the owner a day
 * at worst.
 */
export async function giveBackExport(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string, log: Logger): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await deps.limits.release(exportLimitKey(userId));
  } catch (err) {
    log.warn({ err, userId }, "account export: the day's export could not be given back after a failure before the first byte");
  }
}

const iso = (at: Date): string => at.toISOString();
const isoOrNull = (at: Date | null): string | null => (at ? at.toISOString() : null);

/**
 * What an account module built without the moderation module writes: the member is part of the format, so it is always
 * there. Its reporting counts are empty over the standing rules' frame, the number the moderation module would read.
 */
const NO_MODERATION: ModerationExport = {
  decisions: [],
  reports: [],
  strikes: [],
  standing: [],
  replies: [],
  reporting: { frameDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays, days: [], marks: [], markedReports: 0 },
};

/**
 * Reads what is needed before the first byte: the account's facts, sessions, devices and events (one
 * read, bounded by the 90 days of events), the profile's own fields, the list of images, and the
 * moderation member (the decisions the account was told of and its own reports, both short lists). The
 * four modules are asked at once, so a read that fails costs the owner nothing: no byte was sent yet.
 * `currentSession` is the handle of the session asking, which marks its entry among the sessions.
 * `pageSize` is how many rows of each profile list are read at a time; tests lower it.
 */
export async function buildExport(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string, currentSession: string, now: Date, pageSize?: number): Promise<ExportPlan> {
  const [account, profile, images, moderation] = await Promise.all([
    deps.auth.exportAccount(userId),
    deps.social.exportProfile(userId, pageSize),
    deps.media.exportImages(userId),
    // The server always hands the moderation module over; a test of the other members may leave it out.
    deps.moderation ? deps.moderation.exportFor(userId) : NO_MODERATION,
  ]);
  return { exportedAt: now, currentSession, account, profile, moderation, images, missingMedia: [] };
}

/** A list member of export.json, read in pages and written one element at a time. */
class Paged<T> {
  constructor(
    readonly pages: AsyncIterable<readonly T[]>,
    readonly element: (row: T) => unknown,
  ) {}
}

/** An array already in memory, as one page. */
function inMemory<T>(rows: readonly T[], element: (row: T) => unknown): Paged<T> {
  return new Paged(
    (async function* () {
      yield rows;
    })(),
    element,
  );
}

/** Fragments are gathered into pieces of about this many UTF-16 units, at most 3 bytes each in UTF-8: well under 64 KiB. */
const PIECE_CHARS = 16 * 1024;

/**
 * export.json in pieces, written exactly as JSON.stringify(document, null, 2) writes the whole
 * document: member by member at the top level, and the lists element by element, each element
 * stringified on its own and indented to its depth (JSON.stringify's output holds line breaks only
 * between tokens; one inside a string is escaped, so indenting after every line break is exact). No list
 * is ever whole in memory: each is read page by page as it is written.
 */
export async function* exportJson(plan: ExportPlan): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  let buffer = "";
  for await (const fragment of documentFragments(plan)) {
    buffer += fragment;
    if (buffer.length >= PIECE_CHARS) {
      yield buffer;
      buffer = "";
    }
  }
  if (buffer.length > 0) yield buffer;
}

async function* documentFragments(plan: ExportPlan): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  const { account, profile } = plan;
  const ref = (row: { postId: string; at: Date }) => ({ postId: row.postId, at: iso(row.at) });
  const other = (row: { handle: string; since: Date }) => ({ handle: row.handle, since: iso(row.since) });
  // The members in the order of the format (ExportFormat in the contracts); the order is part of the bytes.
  const members: [string, unknown][] = [
    ["format", "korbat-export-1"],
    ["exportedAt", iso(plan.exportedAt)],
    [
      "account",
      {
        id: account.account.id,
        email: account.account.email,
        createdAt: iso(account.account.createdAt),
        role: account.account.role,
        mfaEnabled: account.account.mfaEnabled,
        hasPassword: account.account.hasPassword,
        verified: account.account.verified,
        termsVersion: account.account.termsVersion,
        termsAcceptedAt: isoOrNull(account.account.termsAcceptedAt),
        // Inside the account, where the format places them; at most the cap of ten, so they are written with the account's other facts rather than paged.
        passkeys: account.passkeys.map((passkey) => ({ name: passkey.name, createdAt: iso(passkey.createdAt), lastUsedAt: isoOrNull(passkey.lastUsedAt), synced: passkey.synced, createdOn: passkey.createdOn })),
      },
    ],
    [
      "profile",
      {
        handle: profile.profile.handle,
        displayName: profile.profile.displayName,
        bio: profile.profile.bio,
        createdAt: iso(profile.profile.createdAt),
        handleHistory: [...profile.profile.handleHistory],
        // Last in the profile, where the format added it (2c); the member order is part of the bytes.
        showInExplore: profile.profile.showInExplore,
        // After it, where 3e added it (W.8): the retired handles of the history, with when.
        retiredHandles: profile.profile.retiredHandles.map((retired) => ({ handle: retired.handle, retiredAt: iso(retired.retiredAt) })),
      },
    ],
    [
      "posts",
      new Paged(profile.posts, (post) => ({
        id: post.id,
        body: post.body,
        createdAt: iso(post.createdAt),
        replyToId: post.replyToId,
        quoteOfId: post.quoteOfId,
        state: post.state,
        deletedAt: isoOrNull(post.deletedAt),
        media: post.media.map((image) => ({ id: image.id, file: mediaEntry(image.id), altText: image.altText, width: image.width, height: image.height })),
      })),
    ],
    ["likes", new Paged(profile.likes, ref)],
    ["reposts", new Paged(profile.reposts, ref)],
    ["bookmarks", new Paged(profile.bookmarks, ref)],
    ["following", new Paged(profile.following, other)],
    ["blocks", new Paged(profile.blocks, other)],
    ["mutes", new Paged(profile.mutes, other)],
    [
      "sessions",
      inMemory(account.sessions, (session) => ({ id: session.id, createdAt: iso(session.createdAt), lastUsedAt: iso(session.lastUsedAt), current: session.id === plan.currentSession })),
    ],
    [
      "devices",
      // The platform column is text; sign-in only ever writes one of the contract's three values.
      inMemory(account.devices, (device) => ({ label: device.label, platform: device.platform as Platform, firstSeenAt: iso(device.firstSeenAt), lastSeenAt: iso(device.lastSeenAt) })),
    ],
    ["events", inMemory(account.events, (event) => ({ type: event.type, at: iso(event.at) }))],
    // Complete by now: the images were written before the JSON.
    ["missingMedia", inMemory(plan.missingMedia, (id) => id)],
    // Last, where the format added it (3c). Each entry is written member by member in the format's order, so the bytes
    // do not depend on how the moderation module builds its objects, and nothing beyond the format is ever written.
    ["moderation", moderationMember(plan.moderation)],
  ];

  yield "{\n";
  for (const [index, [key, value]] of members.entries()) {
    yield `${index === 0 ? "" : ",\n"}  ${JSON.stringify(key)}: `;
    if (value instanceof Paged) yield* listFragments(value);
    else yield indented(JSON.stringify(value, null, 2), "  ");
  }
  yield "\n}";
}

/** The moderation member with every entry's members in the order of the format (ExportFormat in the contracts). */
function moderationMember(moderation: ModerationExport): ModerationExport {
  return {
    decisions: moderation.decisions.map((decision) => ({
      id: decision.id,
      decidedOn: decision.decidedOn,
      postId: decision.postId,
      kind: decision.kind,
      outcome: decision.outcome,
      ground: decision.ground,
      ruleId: decision.ruleId,
      rulesVersion: decision.rulesVersion,
      measures: decision.measures.map((measure) => ({ kind: measure.kind, mediaId: measure.mediaId, noEffect: measure.noEffect })),
      reversals: decision.reversals.map((reversal) => ({ kind: reversal.kind, mediaId: reversal.mediaId })),
      facts: decision.facts,
      reason: decision.reason,
      legalReference: decision.legalReference,
      appeal: decision.appeal === null ? null : decision.appeal.state === "pending" ? { state: "pending", result: null } : { state: "answered", result: decision.appeal.result },
    })),
    reports: moderation.reports.map((report) => ({
      ref: report.ref,
      receivedAt: report.receivedAt,
      ground: report.ground,
      ruleId: report.ruleId,
      category: report.category,
      explanation: report.explanation,
      items: report.items.map((item) => ({ position: item.position, link: item.link, reexamines: item.reexamines, outcome: item.outcome, outcomeText: item.outcomeText, reexaminationOpen: item.reexaminationOpen })),
    })),
    // 3e (W.8): the strikes the account was given.
    strikes: moderation.strikes.map((strike) => ({ decisionId: strike.decisionId, postId: strike.postId, ruleId: strike.ruleId, givenAt: strike.givenAt, countsUntil: strike.countsUntil, overruledAt: strike.overruledAt })),
    // Then its suspensions, terminations and reporting measures, its replies to them, and its own reporting counts.
    standing: moderation.standing.map((entry) => ({
      decisionId: entry.decisionId,
      kind: entry.kind,
      basis: entry.basis,
      days: entry.days,
      announced: entry.announced,
      decidedAt: entry.decidedAt,
      earliestStart: entry.earliestStart,
      startsAt: entry.startsAt,
      endsAt: entry.endsAt,
      liftedAt: entry.liftedAt,
      liftedBy: entry.liftedBy,
      replaced: entry.replaced,
      basisEndedAt: entry.basisEndedAt,
      basisEndedBy: entry.basisEndedBy,
    })),
    replies: moderation.replies.map((reply) => ({ decisionId: reply.decisionId, filedAt: reply.filedAt, onTime: reply.onTime, text: reply.text, erasedAt: reply.erasedAt, answeredAt: reply.answeredAt, answeredBy: reply.answeredBy })),
    reporting: {
      frameDays: moderation.reporting.frameDays,
      days: moderation.reporting.days.map((entry) => ({ day: entry.day, reports: entry.reports })),
      marks: moderation.reporting.marks.map((mark) => ({ ref: mark.ref, position: mark.position, sentOn: mark.sentOn, markedAt: mark.markedAt, withdrawnAt: mark.withdrawnAt, counts: mark.counts })),
      markedReports: moderation.reporting.markedReports,
    },
  };
}

/** A top-level member's array, as JSON.stringify writes it at that depth: "[]" when empty, else one element per line group. */
async function* listFragments<T>(list: Paged<T>): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  let first = true;
  for await (const page of list.pages) {
    for (const row of page) {
      yield `${first ? "[\n" : ",\n"}    ${indented(JSON.stringify(list.element(row), null, 2), "    ")}`;
      first = false;
    }
  }
  yield first ? "[]" : "\n  ]";
}

const indented = (json: string, pad: string): string => json.replaceAll("\n", `\n${pad}`);

/**
 * Writes the archive: every image as a stored entry, then export.json, then the central directory.
 * export.json comes last so that missingMedia can name every image whose file the checked open refused
 * or did not find when its turn came (the sweeper may be between the row and the file), or that was no
 * longer the owner's to export by then: the media module reads each image's row again as it opens the
 * file, and opens none for an image deleted with its post, erased or sealed since the list was read.
 * The order of entries means nothing to a reader.
 */
export async function writeExport(writer: ZipWriter, plan: ExportPlan): Promise<void> {
  for (const image of plan.images) {
    if (!(await writer.addFile(mediaEntry(image.id), image.open))) plan.missingMedia.push(image.id);
  }
  await writer.addJsonPieces("export.json", exportJson(plan));
  await writer.end();
}
```

### Replace `apps/api/src/cli/staff-cases.ts` (whole file)

```ts
/**
 * The staff command line's commands for moderation cases (3c design, section 7.13): link, unlink, limits, text-verify,
 * account-facts and access-request. staff.ts parses their arguments, reads their settings and opens their connections;
 * this file holds what each does, over the connections it is handed. Each sets the 10-second lock timeout in every
 * transaction it opens, writes its audit row in the transaction of its change and as that transaction's last statement
 * (the insert holds the chain's head until the commit), and says so when it changed nothing it was asked to.
 *
 * This file has no entry point of its own, so both bundles can include it (build.mjs says why that matters).
 */
import { and, eq, isNull, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { MEASURE_KINDS, snapshotDigest, textDigest, type SnapshotDigestInput } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { moderationLimits, profiles, staffPersonalAccounts, users, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID } from "../auth";
import { imageModerationStates } from "../media";
import { accessDraftForAccount, accessDraftForContacts, type AccountAccessDraft, type ContactsAccessDraft } from "../moderation";
import { appendAuditRow } from "../staff";

/** What a command reads and writes through: its own connection, or a transaction a test hands in. */
type Runner = Db | DbTx;

const rowsOf = async <T>(q: Runner, query: ReturnType<typeof sql>): Promise<T[]> => (await q.execute(query)) as unknown as T[];
const uuidArray = (ids: readonly string[]) => sql`${`{${ids.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]`;
const textArray = (values: readonly string[]) => sql`${`{${values.join(",")}}`}::text[]`;

/** Runs `change` in a transaction that waits at most 10 seconds for a lock, as every staff command waits. */
function changing<T>(db: Runner, change: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
    return change(tx);
  });
}

/** A handle as the operator types it, with or without its at sign, in the lower case the profiles hold. */
export const handleArg = (arg: string): string => arg.replace(/^@/, "").toLowerCase();

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- link and unlink

export type Changed = { ok: true; lines: string[] } | { ok: false; problem: string };

/**
 * Records, or with `remove` takes back, that a personal account is a staff member's own (the recusal check of 3c reads
 * the links; no API role can). As the migrator, in one transaction: the staff account's row and the personal account's
 * are locked FOR SHARE, so neither can be promoted, demoted or taken down under the check; a link is recorded only for
 * a live staff account and a live account that is not staff. The audit row names the staff account and nothing of the
 * link, which must not spread.
 */
export async function changeLink(migrateDb: Runner, staffEmail: string, personalHandle: string, remove: boolean): Promise<Changed> {
  const handle = handleArg(personalHandle);
  return changing(migrateDb, async (tx): Promise<Changed> => {
    const [staff] = await tx
      .select({ id: users.id, role: users.role })
      .from(users)
      .where(and(sql`lower(${users.email}) = lower(${staffEmail})`, isNull(users.deletedAt)))
      .limit(1)
      .for("share");
    if (!staff) return { ok: false, problem: `no live account for ${staffEmail}` };
    const [profile] = await tx.select({ id: profiles.id }).from(profiles).where(eq(profiles.handle, handle)).limit(1);
    if (!profile) return { ok: false, problem: `no account has the handle @${handle}` };
    if (remove) {
      const gone = await tx.delete(staffPersonalAccounts).where(and(eq(staffPersonalAccounts.staffUserId, staff.id), eq(staffPersonalAccounts.personalUserId, profile.id))).returning({ id: staffPersonalAccounts.staffUserId });
      if (gone.length === 0) return { ok: false, problem: `@${handle} is not linked to ${staffEmail}; nothing changed` };
      await appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "staff_link_removed", targetType: "user", targetId: staff.id, requestId: null, metadata: {} });
      return { ok: true, lines: [`unlink: @${handle} is no longer linked to ${staffEmail}. Update your own record of this staff member's linked handles.`] };
    }
    if (staff.role === "user") return { ok: false, problem: `${staffEmail} is not staff (its role is user)` };
    const [personal] = await tx.select({ id: users.id, role: users.role, deletedAt: users.deletedAt }).from(users).where(eq(users.id, profile.id)).limit(1).for("share");
    if (!personal || personal.deletedAt !== null) return { ok: false, problem: `@${handle} is not a live account` };
    if (personal.id === staff.id) return { ok: false, problem: `@${handle} is the staff account itself, which is always a party where it is one` };
    if (personal.role !== "user") return { ok: false, problem: `@${handle} is a staff account (its role is ${personal.role}); only a personal account is linked` };
    const added = await tx.insert(staffPersonalAccounts).values({ staffUserId: staff.id, personalUserId: personal.id }).onConflictDoNothing().returning({ id: staffPersonalAccounts.staffUserId });
    if (added.length === 0) return { ok: false, problem: `@${handle} is already linked to ${staffEmail}; nothing changed` };
    await appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "staff_link_added", targetType: "user", targetId: staff.id, requestId: null, metadata: {} });
    return { ok: true, lines: [`link: @${handle} is linked to ${staffEmail}. Update your own record of this staff member's linked handles.`] };
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- limits

/** The five limits on staff, in the order the command takes them. */
export interface StaffLimits {
  decisionsPerHour: number;
  decisionsPerDay: number;
  caseOpensPerDay: number;
  findingsPerDay: number;
  revealsPerDay: number;
}

const describeLimits = (l: StaffLimits) => `${l.decisionsPerHour} decisions an hour, ${l.decisionsPerDay} decisions a day, ${l.caseOpensPerDay} case opens a day, ${l.findingsPerDay} findings a day, ${l.revealsPerDay} reveals a day`;

/**
 * Sets the limits' one row, as the migrator: an upsert, so it also works on a database whose row is missing, that
 * changes the row only when one of the five numbers differs. Its audit row carries the five numbers and is written only
 * when the row was inserted or changed.
 */
export async function setLimits(migrateDb: Runner, limits: StaffLimits): Promise<Changed> {
  return changing(migrateDb, async (tx): Promise<Changed> => {
    const l = moderationLimits;
    const written = await tx
      .insert(l)
      .values({ id: 1, ...limits, updatedAt: sql`now()` })
      .onConflictDoUpdate({
        target: l.id,
        set: { ...limits, updatedAt: sql`now()` },
        setWhere: sql`(${l.decisionsPerHour}, ${l.decisionsPerDay}, ${l.caseOpensPerDay}, ${l.findingsPerDay}, ${l.revealsPerDay}) is distinct from
                      (${limits.decisionsPerHour}::int, ${limits.decisionsPerDay}::int, ${limits.caseOpensPerDay}::int, ${limits.findingsPerDay}::int, ${limits.revealsPerDay}::int)`,
      })
      .returning({ id: l.id });
    if (written.length === 0) return { ok: false, problem: `the limits already are ${describeLimits(limits)}; nothing changed` };
    await appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "moderation_limits_set", targetType: null, targetId: null, requestId: null, metadata: { ...limits } });
    return { ok: true, lines: [`limits: set to ${describeLimits(limits)}. Keep these numbers in your own records: a restore brings back the ones of its backup.`] };
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- account-facts

/**
 * Prints an account's handle, address and creation time for the runbook's Art. 18 step, as the migrator, and records
 * that it did. Only for the subject of the named case: the account the case is about, or the author of its post.
 */
export async function accountFacts(migrateDb: Runner, handleGiven: string, caseId: string): Promise<Changed> {
  const handle = handleArg(handleGiven);
  return changing(migrateDb, async (tx): Promise<Changed> => {
    const [profile] = await tx.select({ id: profiles.id, handle: profiles.handle }).from(profiles).where(eq(profiles.handle, handle)).limit(1);
    if (!profile) return { ok: false, problem: `no account has the handle @${handle}` };
    const [subject] = await rowsOf<{ subject: string | null }>(
      tx,
      sql`select case when c.target_type = 'account' then c.target_id else (select p.author_id from posts p where p.id = c.target_id) end as subject from cases c where c.id = ${caseId}::uuid`,
    );
    if (!subject) return { ok: false, problem: `no case has the id ${caseId}` };
    if (subject.subject !== profile.id) return { ok: false, problem: `@${handle} is not the subject of case ${caseId}; nothing was read` };
    const [account] = await tx.select({ email: users.email, createdAt: users.createdAt }).from(users).where(eq(users.id, profile.id)).limit(1);
    if (!account) return { ok: false, problem: `@${handle} has no account row` };
    await appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "account_facts_read", targetType: "user", targetId: profile.id, requestId: null, metadata: { caseId } });
    return {
      ok: true,
      lines: [
        `handle: @${profile.handle}`,
        `email: ${account.email}`,
        `account created: ${account.createdAt.toISOString()}`,
        "Keep this off the server, with your R2 or Art. 18 record of the case, and destroy it after an answer without a seal (README, runbook).",
      ],
    };
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- access-request

/**
 * Drafts the moderation part of an answer to a GDPR access request and records that it did, on the API role: for a
 * handle the account's cases and its own reports, for an address the notices of the contacts the auth module found for
 * it (`contactsOf`, which alone can read a contact). The audit row carries counts only, and names the account for a
 * handle and nobody for an address.
 */
export async function accessRequest(
  apiDb: Runner,
  appOrigin: string,
  who: { handle: string } | { email: string },
  contactsOf: (email: string) => Promise<{ id: string; name: string | null }[]>,
): Promise<{ ok: true; draft: AccountAccessDraft | ContactsAccessDraft } | { ok: false; problem: string }> {
  if ("handle" in who) {
    const handle = handleArg(who.handle);
    const [profile] = await apiDb.select({ id: profiles.id, handle: profiles.handle }).from(profiles).where(eq(profiles.handle, handle)).limit(1);
    if (!profile) return { ok: false, problem: `no account has the handle @${handle}` };
    const draft = await accessDraftForAccount(apiDb, appOrigin, profile);
    await changing(apiDb, (tx) => appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "access_request_drafted", targetType: "user", targetId: profile.id, requestId: null, metadata: { cases: draft.cases.length, contacts: 0 } }));
    return { ok: true, draft };
  }
  const contacts = await contactsOf(who.email);
  const draft = await accessDraftForContacts(apiDb, appOrigin, contacts);
  await changing(apiDb, (tx) => appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "access_request_drafted", targetType: null, targetId: null, requestId: null, metadata: { cases: 0, contacts: contacts.length } }));
  return { ok: true, draft };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- text-verify

/** One thing text-verify found wrong, and what it is about: an audit row by its place, or a decision, a post, an image or a seal by its id. */
export interface TextProblem {
  about: "audit" | "decision" | "post" | "image" | "seal";
  id: string;
  message: string;
}

export interface TextReport {
  ok: boolean;
  /** The confirmed rows read, and the decisions, posts, images and seals in force checked. */
  auditRows: number;
  decisions: number;
  posts: number;
  images: number;
  seals: number;
  /** The first problems, in the order found. */
  problems: TextProblem[];
  problemCount: number;
}

/** How many rows text-verify reads at a time. */
export const TEXT_VERIFY_PAGE_SIZE = 1000;
const PAGE = TEXT_VERIFY_PAGE_SIZE;

/** The actions whose params name saved texts and snapshots by their digests. */
const CONFIRMED_ACTIONS = ["case_decided", "appeals_reviewed", "identity_revealed"];
/** The params members that name a saved text. */
const TEXT_MEMBERS = ["factsDigest", "reasonDigest", "legalReferenceDigest"];

interface NamingRow {
  place: number;
  action: string;
  actorId: string;
  targetType: string | null;
  targetId: string | null;
  params: Record<string, unknown>;
}

const isObject = (value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> => typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
/** An action as the key signed it and as the ledger holds it: its kind, its image, and (3e) the days and whether it was announced. */
const actionKey = (action: { kind: unknown; mediaId: unknown; days?: unknown; announced?: unknown }) =>
  [action.kind, action.mediaId, action.days, action.announced].map((part) => (part === null || part === undefined ? "" : String(part))).join(":");

/**
 * text-verify (3c design, section 7.13), read-only on the API's role. audit-verify proves that the record was not
 * rewritten; this proves that what the record's confirmed rows name is still what korbat holds, and that what posts and
 * images show is what the record says. Three checks, each in this command's own code:
 *
 *   1. Every digest in the params of a confirmed row (a decision, a review, a reveal) names a saved text that korbat
 *      still holds and that recomputes to it, an erased text, a snapshot still held that recomputes to it, or an erased
 *      snapshot. A text or a snapshot that is missing was removed around the erasures, which keep each row and its digest.
 *   2. Every decision is named by exactly one such row, written by the deciding account on the decision's case (for a
 *      review, on the reviewed decision), whose params equal the decision's own columns and whose actions equal its
 *      ledger rows as a set (3e: with each row's days and whether it was announced; the marks the decision set equal the
 *      params' `unfounded`, and a withdrawal for another measure its `replaced`). A signed mark that korbat's own rules
 *      deleted is no difference: its report was sent on a UTC day before the frame of the reporting counts (the
 *      retention job's step), or korbat no longer knows who sent the report (the sender's account was purged, which
 *      deletes its marks; an intake whose record was erased also forgets its sender, so a mark deleted by hand from such
 *      a report is not told apart). A row that names a decision korbat does not hold is reported too.
 *   3. Every post's level and every image's state equal what the ledger of measures gives, worked out here from the
 *      ledger's rows, the cases' closures, the items and the erasure marks, as the database's own writer derives them;
 *      and every post a seal in force lists still has the number of image rows the seal recorded.
 *
 * So a change made around the triggers, by the migrator or by hand, is reported: a decision or a measure altered or
 * removed, a level or a state set, a sealed image row destroyed or lost in a restore. `keep` bounds the problems kept.
 */
export async function textVerify(q: Runner, keep = 100): Promise<TextReport> {
  const problems: TextProblem[] = [];
  let problemCount = 0;
  const problem = (about: TextProblem["about"], id: string, message: string) => {
    problemCount++;
    if (problems.length < keep) problems.push({ about, id, message });
  };

  // ---- 1. the confirmed rows and what their digests name
  const naming = new Map<string, NamingRow[]>();
  let auditRows = 0;
  for (let after = 0; ; ) {
    const page = await rowsOf<{ id: number; place: number; action: string; actor_id: string; target_type: string | null; target_id: string | null; metadata: unknown }>(
      q,
      sql`select id::int as id, chain_seq::int as place, action, actor_id, target_type, target_id, metadata from audit_log
           where action = any(${textArray(CONFIRMED_ACTIONS)}) and id > ${after} order by id limit ${PAGE}`,
    );
    const wanted: { place: number; member: string; digest: string }[] = [];
    const wantedSnapshots: { place: number; id: string; digest: string }[] = [];
    for (const row of page) {
      auditRows++;
      const metadata = isObject(row.metadata) ? row.metadata : {};
      const params = isObject(metadata.params) ? metadata.params : null;
      if (params === null) {
        problem("audit", String(row.place), `its action, ${row.action}, carries no params`);
        continue;
      }
      for (const member of TEXT_MEMBERS) if (typeof params[member] === "string") wanted.push({ place: row.place, member, digest: params[member] });
      if (typeof params.snapshotId === "string" && typeof params.snapshotDigest === "string") wantedSnapshots.push({ place: row.place, id: params.snapshotId, digest: params.snapshotDigest });
      if (row.action !== "identity_revealed") {
        const decisionId = typeof metadata.decisionId === "string" ? metadata.decisionId : null;
        if (decisionId === null) problem("audit", String(row.place), `its action, ${row.action}, names no decision`);
        else naming.set(decisionId, [...(naming.get(decisionId) ?? []), { place: row.place, action: row.action, actorId: row.actor_id, targetType: row.target_type, targetId: row.target_id, params }]);
      }
    }
    if (wanted.length > 0) {
      const texts = await rowsOf<{ digest: string; text: string | null; salt: string | null }>(q, sql`select digest, text, salt from staff_texts where digest = any(${textArray([...new Set(wanted.map((w) => w.digest))])})`);
      const byDigest = new Map(texts.map((t) => [t.digest, t]));
      for (const w of wanted) {
        const held = byDigest.get(w.digest);
        if (!held) problem("audit", String(w.place), `its ${w.member} names no saved text`);
        // An erased text keeps its row and its digest: that is retention at work, and nothing to report.
        else if (held.text !== null && (held.salt === null || (await textDigest(held.salt, held.text).catch(() => null)) !== w.digest)) problem("audit", String(w.place), `the text its ${w.member} names no longer recomputes to that digest`);
      }
    }
    if (wantedSnapshots.length > 0) {
      const found = await rowsOf<Record<string, unknown> & { id: string; digest: string; erased: boolean }>(
        q,
        sql`select id, digest, erased_at is not null as erased, salt, target_type::text as target_type, target_id,
                   to_char(taken_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as taken_at, author_handle, post_state::text as post_state,
                   to_char(post_created_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as post_created_at, reply_to_id, quote_of_id, body, media, display_name, bio, handle
              from evidence_snapshots where id = any(${uuidArray([...new Set(wantedSnapshots.map((w) => w.id))])})`,
      );
      const byId = new Map(found.map((s) => [s.id, s]));
      for (const w of wantedSnapshots) {
        const s = byId.get(w.id);
        if (!s) problem("audit", String(w.place), "its snapshotId names no snapshot");
        else if (s.digest !== w.digest) problem("audit", String(w.place), "its snapshotDigest is not the digest of the snapshot it names");
        else if (!s.erased) {
          const input = { salt: s.salt, targetType: s.target_type, targetId: s.target_id, takenAt: s.taken_at, authorHandle: s.author_handle, postState: s.post_state, postCreatedAt: s.post_created_at, replyToId: s.reply_to_id, quoteOfId: s.quote_of_id, body: s.body, media: s.media, displayName: s.display_name, bio: s.bio, handle: s.handle } as unknown as SnapshotDigestInput;
          if ((await snapshotDigest(input).catch(() => null)) !== w.digest) problem("audit", String(w.place), "the snapshot it names no longer recomputes to its digest");
        }
      }
    }
    if (page.length < PAGE) break;
    after = page[page.length - 1]!.id;
  }

  // ---- 2. every decision against the one row that names it
  let decisions = 0;
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (let after: string | null = null; ; ) {
    const page: { id: string; d: Record<string, unknown>; actions: { kind: string; mediaId: string | null; days: number | null; announced: boolean | null }[]; marks: string[]; forgotten: string[]; replaced: boolean }[] = await rowsOf(
      q,
      sql`select d.id, to_jsonb(d) as d,
                 coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('kind', a.kind, 'mediaId', a.media_id, 'days', a.days, 'announced', a.announced)) from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id), '[]'::jsonb) as actions,
                 coalesce((select jsonb_agg(m.item_id) from unfounded_marks m where m.decision_id = d.id), '[]'::jsonb) as marks,
                 coalesce((select jsonb_agg(i.id) from intake_items i join intakes n on n.id = i.intake_id
                            where i.answered_by = d.id
                              and ((n.received_at at time zone 'UTC')::date <= (now() at time zone 'UTC')::date - (select k.report_frame_days from standing_rules() k)
                                   or n.reporter_id is null)), '[]'::jsonb) as forgotten,
                 exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.replaced) as replaced
            from decisions d where ${after === null ? sql`true` : sql`d.id > ${after}::uuid`} order by d.id limit ${PAGE}`,
    );
    for (const { id, d, actions, marks, forgotten, replaced } of page) {
      decisions++;
      seen.add(id);
      const named = naming.get(id) ?? [];
      if (named.length !== 1) {
        problem("decision", id, named.length === 0 ? "no confirmed row of the audit log names it" : `${named.length} rows of the audit log name it (places ${named.map((row) => row.place).join(", ")})`);
        continue;
      }
      const row = named[0]!;
      const review = d.kind === "review";
      const expected: Record<string, unknown> = review
        ? { stateVersion: d.seen_state_version, appealId: d.appeal_id, snapshotId: d.snapshot_id, snapshotDigest: d.snapshot_digest, outcome: d.outcome, rulesVersion: d.rules_version, redressVersion: d.redress_version, category: d.category, reasonDigest: d.reason_digest }
        : {
            kind: d.kind, stateVersion: d.seen_state_version, throughSeq: d.through_seq, reviewsDecisionId: d.reviews_decision_id, snapshotId: d.snapshot_id, snapshotDigest: d.snapshot_digest, outcome: d.outcome,
            ground: d.ground, ruleId: d.rule_id, rulesVersion: d.rules_version, redressVersion: d.redress_version, category: d.category, categoryKeyword: d.category_keyword,
            factsDigest: d.facts_digest, reasonDigest: d.reason_digest, legalReferenceDigest: d.legal_reference_digest,
          };
      const differing: string[] = [];
      if (row.actorId !== d.decided_by) differing.push("actor");
      if (row.action !== (review ? "appeals_reviewed" : "case_decided") || row.targetType !== (review ? "decision" : "case") || row.targetId !== (review ? d.reviews_decision_id : d.case_id)) differing.push("target");
      for (const key of new Set([...Object.keys(expected), ...Object.keys(row.params)])) {
        if (key === "actions" || key === "unfounded" || key === "replaced") continue;
        if ((expected[key] ?? null) !== (row.params[key] ?? null)) differing.push(key);
        if (!(key in expected)) differing.push(key);
      }
      // 3e: the marks the decision set, as the sorted item ids its params signed, and whether it withdrew a suspension for
      // another measure; a review signs neither, and a row signed before 3e lacks both, which reads as none and false.
      if (!review) {
        const signed = row.params.unfounded === undefined ? [] : Array.isArray(row.params.unfounded) ? row.params.unfounded.map(String) : null;
        // 3e Task 7: a signed mark with no row is no difference when korbat's own rules may have deleted it (above).
        const held = new Set(marks);
        const expected = signed?.filter((item) => held.has(item) || !forgotten.includes(item));
        if (expected === undefined || [...expected].sort().join("|") !== [...marks].sort().join("|")) differing.push("unfounded");
        if ((row.params.replaced ?? false) !== replaced) differing.push("replaced");
      }
      const recorded = Array.isArray(row.params.actions) ? row.params.actions.filter(isObject).map((a) => actionKey({ kind: a.kind, mediaId: a.mediaId, days: a.days, announced: a.announced })) : null;
      if (recorded === null || [...recorded].sort().join("|") !== actions.map(actionKey).sort().join("|")) differing.push("actions");
      if (differing.length > 0) problem("decision", id, `it differs from the audit row at place ${row.place} that names it: ${[...new Set(differing)].sort().join(", ")}`);
    }
    if (page.length < PAGE) break;
    after = page[page.length - 1]!.id;
  }
  for (const [decisionId, named] of naming) if (!seen.has(decisionId)) problem("decision", decisionId, `the audit row at place ${named[0]!.place} names it, and korbat holds no such decision`);

  // ---- 3. levels and states, worked out from the ledger
  const measures = MEASURE_KINDS as readonly string[];
  const removedPosts = new Set<string>();
  const withheldPosts = new Set<string>();
  const removedImages = new Set<string>();
  const withheldImages = new Set<string>();
  const sealsInForce = new Set<string>();
  for (let after: string | null = null; ; ) {
    const page: { id: string; kind: string; post_id: string | null; media_id: string | null; decision_kind: string; case_open: boolean; suspect_open: boolean; reversed: boolean }[] = await rowsOf(
      q,
      sql`select a.id, a.kind::text as kind, a.post_id, a.media_id, d.kind::text as decision_kind, c.closed_at is null as case_open,
                 exists (select 1 from intake_items i where i.case_id = d.case_id and i.suspect and i.answered_by is null and i.created_at <= d.decided_at) as suspect_open,
                 exists (select 1 from decision_actions r where r.reverses_action_id = a.id) as reversed
            from decision_actions a join decisions d on d.id = a.decision_id join cases c on c.id = d.case_id
           where a.kind::text = any(${textArray(measures)}) and ${after === null ? sql`true` : sql`a.id > ${after}::uuid`} order by a.id limit ${PAGE}`,
    );
    for (const m of page) {
      // In force: no row reverses it, and a measure taken while deciding lasts while its case is open, a seal taken while
      // deciding while its case holds an unanswered suspect item that arrived no later than it.
      const inForce = !m.reversed && (m.decision_kind !== "interim" || (m.kind === "seal_media" ? m.suspect_open : m.case_open));
      if (!inForce) continue;
      if (m.kind === "remove" && m.post_id) removedPosts.add(m.post_id);
      else if (m.kind === "withhold" && m.post_id) withheldPosts.add(m.post_id);
      else if (m.kind === "remove_media" && m.media_id) removedImages.add(m.media_id);
      else if (m.kind === "withhold_media" && m.media_id) withheldImages.add(m.media_id);
      else if (m.kind === "seal_media") sealsInForce.add(m.id);
    }
    if (page.length < PAGE) break;
    after = page[page.length - 1]!.id;
  }
  // The posts each seal in force lists, with the image rows it recorded for each.
  const listed: { actionId: string; postId: string; images: number }[] = [];
  const sealedPosts = new Set<string>();
  if (sealsInForce.size > 0) {
    const found = await rowsOf<{ action_id: string; post_id: string; images: number }>(q, sql`select action_id, post_id, images::int as images from seal_posts where action_id = any(${uuidArray([...sealsInForce])}) order by action_id, post_id`);
    for (const row of found) {
      listed.push({ actionId: row.action_id, postId: row.post_id, images: row.images });
      sealedPosts.add(row.post_id);
    }
  }

  let posts = 0;
  for (let after: string | null = null; ; ) {
    const page: { id: string; state: string; level: string; erased: boolean }[] = await rowsOf(
      q,
      sql`select id, state::text as state, moderation_level::text as level, erased_at is not null as erased from posts where ${after === null ? sql`true` : sql`id > ${after}::uuid`} order by id limit ${PAGE}`,
    );
    for (const post of page) {
      posts++;
      const level = post.erased || removedPosts.has(post.id) ? "removed" : withheldPosts.has(post.id) ? "withheld" : "visible";
      if (post.level !== level) problem("post", post.id, `its level is stored as ${post.level}, and the ledger of measures gives ${level}`);
      // The state mirrors the level unless the author deleted the post, which is terminal.
      else if (post.state !== "deleted_by_author" && post.state !== level) problem("post", post.id, `its state is stored as ${post.state}, and its level is ${level}`);
    }
    if (page.length < PAGE) break;
    after = page[page.length - 1]!.id;
  }

  let images = 0;
  const imagesOn = new Map<string, number>();
  for (let after: string | null = null; ; ) {
    const page = await imageModerationStates(q as Db, after, PAGE);
    for (const image of page) {
      images++;
      if (sealedPosts.has(image.postId)) imagesOn.set(image.postId, (imagesOn.get(image.postId) ?? 0) + 1);
      const state = sealedPosts.has(image.postId) ? "sealed" : image.erasedAt !== null || removedImages.has(image.id) ? "removed" : withheldImages.has(image.id) ? "withheld" : "visible";
      if (image.moderationState !== state) problem("image", image.id, `its state is stored as ${image.moderationState}, and the ledger of measures gives ${state}`);
    }
    if (page.length < PAGE) break;
    after = page[page.length - 1]!.id;
  }
  for (const row of listed) {
    const now = imagesOn.get(row.postId) ?? 0;
    if (now !== row.images) problem("seal", row.actionId, `it lists post ${row.postId} with ${row.images} image ${row.images === 1 ? "row" : "rows"}, and the post has ${now} now`);
  }

  return { ok: problemCount === 0, auditRows, decisions, posts, images, seals: sealsInForce.size, problems, problemCount };
}

/** text-verify on the command line's own connection: one REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY transaction, so every check reads one state of the database. */
export function textVerifyOn(apiDb: Db): Promise<TextReport> {
  return apiDb.transaction(
    async (tx) => {
      await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
      return textVerify(tx);
    },
    { isolationLevel: "repeatable read", accessMode: "read only" },
  );
}

/** How text-verify reports: what holds, or the first problems. */
export function describeTextReport(report: TextReport): string[] {
  const counted = `${report.auditRows} confirmed rows, ${report.decisions} decisions, ${report.posts} posts, ${report.images} images and ${report.seals} seals in force`;
  if (report.ok) return [`text-verify: what the record names is what korbat holds: ${counted}`];
  const shown = report.problems.slice(0, 20);
  const lines = [`text-verify: FAILED, ${report.problemCount} ${report.problemCount === 1 ? "problem" : "problems"} in ${counted}; the first:`];
  for (const p of shown) lines.push(`  ${p.about === "audit" ? "place" : p.about} ${p.id}: ${p.message}`);
  if (report.problemCount > shown.length) lines.push(`  and ${report.problemCount - shown.length} more`);
  return lines;
}
```
